summary.text: One of the brothers of Antiphus — the warrior the Cyclops slew in his cave — who himself consorted with Penelope's suitors while two other brothers kept their father's farm; among the last and bravest wooers when the bow had already slain the rest.

story.text: Telemachus, opening the assembly on Ithaca, mourned Antiphus the warrior, whom the savage Cyclops had slain in his cave. Three brothers remained: Eurynomus consorted with the wooers, and two ever kept their father's farm — yet the prince could not forget the one lost.
In the last battle of the hall he stood with Agelaus, Amphimedon, Demoptolemus, Peisander and wise Polybus when the rest had fallen to the bow — and fought on until Odysseus and his men prevailed.
Apollodorus names Eurynomus among the twelve suitors from Ithaca itself.
